newsitem.title: UK: Coffee market seen stable in 96 -- UK coffee chief.
newsitem.headline: Coffee market seen stable in 96 -- UK coffee chief.

text.p: The coffee market is seeing a reasonable degree of stability in 1996, providing the industry a vital "breathing space" after two years of volatility, the head of the UK Coffee Federation said.

"On balance, the year has witnessed a reasonable degree of stability within our industry which hopefully has provided that all-important breathing space when fences, where necessary can, and have, been repaired," Anthony Miller, the federation's executive chairman said.
Miller's remarks were made in a prepared text delivered at the federation's 46th annual dinner in London late on Friday.
Coffee saw a turbulent period in 1994 when frosts and drought hit top grower Brazil, pushing prices to near 10-year highs of $4,140 a tonne.
The two devastating frosts wiped out more than one-third of Brazil's harvest in 1994.
Coffee is now trading about $1,500 a tonne.
Miller also spoke of the growing imports of robusta coffee from key Asian producers into the UK, principally a consumer of the arabica variety.
He said Indonesia, Vietnam and Thailand now accounted for 32 percent of annual UK coffee imports of about 1.85 million 60-kg bags in 1996.
This is sharply higher from about 22 percent in 1995. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
